ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (black/dark grey); high-intensity (white) pixels are limited to approximately <10% of the visible surface area.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: A prominent contiguous high-intensity horizontal linear feature is located in the medial-to-distal region of the right lobe; sparse, non-contiguous white micro-mottling is distributed across the lower margins of both lobes against the uniform dark background.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped depression with an approximate pixel-calculated vertex angle of 65 degrees, dividing the lobes symmetrically.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Continuous irregular serration; low-amplitude variations characterize the inner trailing edge near the notch, while high-amplitude peaks and jagged valleys are concentrated on the terminal distal tips of both lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Trailing edges follow a primary convex curve originating from the median notch, tapering toward the distal tips with moderate upward sweep.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Localized high-contrast circular pixel clusters are detected at the extreme distal tips and along segments of the trailing edge, primarily on the right lobe.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Complex network of unaligned linear disruptions; features a dominant, wide horizontal high-intensity scar on the right lobe intersected by multiple thin, vertical linear marks (rake marks).

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Major horizontal linear scar on the right lobe; vertical rake marks on the medial right lobe; ragged and irregular margins at both distal tips consistent with historical structural loss.
other_distinctive_markers: Unique cross-hatch pattern on the mid-right lobe where a primary horizontal scar is perpendicularly intersected by at least three distinct vertical linear abrasions.
